title: Hom localization for stratified dualizable condensed sheaves on qcqs schemes
statement:
Let $Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], put $R=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$ and choose $t\in R$. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B=p_Y^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $\Lambda[t^{-1}]$ be the condensed ring obtained by inverting $t$, whose underlying module sheaf is the filtered colimit of repeated multiplication by $t$ on $\Lambda$, equipped with the localization ring structure, and put $B'=p_Y^*(\Lambda[t^{-1}])=B[t^{-1}]$. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(B)$ and $D(B')$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with ordinary relative derived tensor [def-weil-derived-tensor].

Let $\mathcal T_\Lambda(Y)$ be the full subcategory of $D(B)$ on objects $M$ admitting a finite stratification of $Y$ by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification] such that the derived restriction of $M$ to every stratum is dualizable for the ordinary derived tensor. Here dualizable means that there are an object $D$ and maps $D\otimes M\to B$ and $B\to M\otimes D$ whose two contraction composites are the identities, with associators and unitors inserted [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Strata and duals may depend on $M$. For every $M,N\in\mathcal T_\Lambda(Y)$ and every integer $r$, the canonical map
$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(M,N[r])\otimes_R R[t^{-1}]
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B')}(B'\otimes_B^L M,(B'\otimes_B^L N)[r])
$$
is bijective. It sends $f/t^n$ to $t^{-n}(1\otimes f)$, is natural in $M,N$, and respects identities and composition. Equivalently, extension of scalars induces a fully faithful functor from the raw scalar localization $\mathcal T_\Lambda(Y)[1/t]$ [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] to $D(B')$. Its tensor and unit comparisons are the canonical balanced tensor isomorphisms, and are compatible with associativity, symmetry, units and restriction along morphisms of qcqs schemes. No Noetherian or finite-dimensional hypothesis on $Y$ is imposed, and no idempotent completion or essential-surjectivity assertion is included.

source.place: Section 5.3, Proposition 5.5 and its proof using Lemma 5.3; the displayed Hom comparison in that proof, passed to homotopy categories and specialized to powers of one scalar. Definition 3.3 gives stratified dualizability. Balanced-tensor coherence and qcqs restriction are the canonical scalar-extension formulation.
